brief: A bracket to hang my 40-inch TV on the living room wall.

requirements.evidence: 3-cell x 2-storey cluster (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full + level 1) with 5x French cleat x2 accessories on rear/side outside faces; check_build ok, meshClash clear. Wall screws / wall strip not modelled.

2x hook plates (accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#0,1#4) on front faces as hang points for TV-side hardware; no VESA hole pattern, no TV prop in catalog to verify against. Build is ~367 mm wide vs ~900 mm wide 40-in TV.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell, 2-storey bracket with French cleats for wall hanging and hook plates as TV-side hang points; capped and locked, checks clear. It cannot be claimed to safely hold a 40-inch TV: Hex Cluster parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material, the configurator checks fit/collisions only, and nothing here verifies strength, load rating, fasteners, wall type or VESA compatibility. Do not hang a TV on it without independent structural verification; use a rated commercial TV mount for a 40-inch set.

lines.key: #8 (4 mm) countersunk wood screw, cleat strip
lines.label: #8 (4 mm) countersunk wood screw, cleat strip
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 5 FRENCH CLEATS: screw each cleat strip to the wall with its bevel on top, sloping down toward the wall, into a stud or a fixing rated for the load, then hang the cell so its hook drops in behind the bevel.
The list gives one printed strip per cleat. For a long run, rip a timber batten to the strip's bevel and hang several cells from it instead.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A side connector joins two bases that stand side by side on the same storey. Bases that touch with no connector on the wall between them are one body (joint bolts); every wall between two groups needs a connector, walls inside a group stay bare. get_build lists each touching wall and the groups. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
